note: Medicine Bow NF campground in a bend of LaBonte Creek at the end of LaBonte Canyon in the Laramie Peak area, about 30 miles southwest of Douglas. The last miles are gravel, easy by car when dry; after moderate or heavy rain the roads in generally need 4WD for a few days until they dry. The LaBonte Canyon OHV trail starts at the back of the campground. No horses. --Claude
summary: FS page (updated 2026-05-22) + rec.gov facility, rates and catalog read: 6 gravel trailer sites (28-36 ft, site 4 55 ft), site 5 FCFS only, $14 (2026 and 2027), 14-night max, vault toilet + pump water, 2027 fee season 05-20 to 11-01 with free off-season use. Sites, facilities, booking, fees written; season left unset. Not waterfront holds (creek under canopy). Pin good. Phone empty -> 307-358-4690. Note rewritten with the after-rain 4WD caveat.
flags: ACCESS (not a drop as worded, same as 6470): rec.gov 'The roads leading into the campground generally require a 4-wheel drive vehicle following a moderate or heavy rain event. They dry quickly and are most often passable by car again within a few days.' with directions 'easily accessible by car when dry'. Weather-conditional, not a standing 4WD recommendation; kept in the note. Reviewer may judge.

OHV: rec.gov 'the LaBonte Canyon Trail starts at the back of the campground, and The Big Bear Trail System is located just 1/4 mile up the canyon' (50-inch trails). A general creekside campground with an OHV trail at the back, not an OHV staging camp - flagged, not dropped.

WATERFRONT stored 'not waterfront': HOLDS. rec.gov says the sites are 'tucked into a bend of the LaBonte Creek', but on Esri the canyon floor beside the loop is continuous conifer canopy and no water is visible; nothing names a site at the creek. Lead only: a site photo naming a creekside site could earn 'creekside'.
SITES: max_rig_ft 36 -> 55 (site 4 lists 55 ft; others 28-36). FS page: 'this campground will be undergoing continual improvements to increase campsites for larger campers.'

SEASON left unset: the FS page's two statements disagree ('Open season is mid-May to early November' vs 'Seasons of Use: June - October'), the campground stays open free in winter as access permits, and a rec.gov rate season (2027: 05-20 to 11-01) is not a campground season.
